answer: Sybil resistance rests on a staked identity beacon: each agent must lock a forfeitable bond tied to one hardware-backed key before it can cast a vote. The haven of trusted agents is therefore finite - every seat costs real capital up front. To cast a thousand fake votes an attacker must lock a thousand separate bonds, and a slashing rule burns the full stake of any agent caught double-signing or obeying one controller. That turns the canyon between honest and fraudulent participation into a steep, capital-denominated cost.
